Phainon looked behind him a bit worried - his brows furrowed together. His steps were slightly nervous, staying just ahead of the slower and out of it Mydeimos. The city was cool but their walk wasn't brisk or anything of the sort. Mydei's meandering pace was an immediate source of worry for Phainon. His cat-eared friend never got sick and he wasn't one to show it so openly if he was. Coming back from their nightly gym run to their apartment should of been full of easy going banter. Instead, Phainon kept nervously staring back at Mydei who seemed much more interested in the pavement. He had gotten immediately worse at the gym but refused to leave so Phainon tagged after him like a lost pup as if he was the animal hybrid out of the two.

Mydei's eyes were glassy - his presence was to do everything robotically, his slit eyes focusing on walls and movements like a wild animal rather than his bestest friend for years. His tail - normally hiked just slightly to show his confidence, almost dragged on the ground behind him. The slump in his shoulders as he held his backpack made Phainon's mouth dry with worry. He wanted to call Hyacine, take him to the doctor, something that could give him more than Mydei's dismissive responses.

He was no hybrid - maybe he should call Cipher? They weren't close as Mydei and her, the two cats of the group- but surely she might know something. Staring at their little corner duplex, the white fence that he and Mydei built together, blue eyes focused on hazy gold. "Something's wrong." He choked out. "Please tell me."

Maybe - maybe, Phainon was rather paranoid. He knew he was - having a sickly and now dead brother he had seen the depths sickness could reach. He was a child but he remembered every moment and it haunted him. He didn't like when people were sick and his studies in post-natal care for chimeras seemed almost a given as he grew older. Wanting to take care of the most vulnerable in society - he would help with hybrids as much as normal patients. As a pure human himself, he had only gained knowledge through cases that he was roped in on - including Mydei's mother's case.

Mydeimos was a Kremnoan - a society that had closed itself off to people but some had escaped the authoritarian regime and through his work with the hospital would slowly grow accustomed to such a strange person but also someone who kept up with him. The feline man at first irritated him with the way he spoke about his sick mother - but seeing him truly take care of her realized it was more of a cultural thing and the blond was not shy in showing his love for his mother.

Phainon took care of her - he took care of his brother - but even if the end result was nothing he could stop, he still tried.

That's maybe why Mydei who had moved him in a while ago for 'thanks' being sick drew up such a panic for the white haired man. Phainon couldn't deal with people being sick or even slightly bothered with illnesses he had researched. He had shoved a thermometer in Mydei's mouth multiple times a day much to the feline man's annoyance. He measured it multiple times a day, tried to get Mydei to call out from work - even tried to make him take more vitamins than normal, cutting up fruit and feeding the peeved man who just wanted to be left alone.

Mydei never actually said no - his tail never lashing in anger - but he could see how much it was strange. He didn't know if it was a cat thing to shove off help. Deal with everything themselves, isolate, and never accept assistance. Phainon didn't want him sick, seeing him even slightly uncomfortable sent spikes of genuine anxiety through him. He had constantly adjusted the temperatures, got him his favorite food at the Kremnoan places, everything he could think of for two days. It only kept getting worse and Mydei would just openly stare at him with that look.

Panting softly, skin flushed - eyes trained on him for a uncomfortably long time before he turned his head to bury it in a pillow or something of the sort. He was sweating and would make strange cat-like chirps when he couldn't see Phainon. Despite his annoyance when Phainon was hovering around - he followed Phainon from room to room, ears twitching when he couldn't see him, tracking his movements.

Phainon felt horrible it actually might be a way to perceive threats. He wondered if he was annoying Mydei enough that maybe he should stay at a friend's house.

"...do you want me to leave?" He had asked on day two, voice low.

Mydei's eyes opened up slowly from where his head was rested on the back of the couch. A slow blink, then a uncomfortably panicked noise, Mydei's weak body shooting into a sitting position. Hands in between his bent knees, he looked genuinely confused. "I..I told you what's wrong with me you can't catch." He said lowly. "Am...I bothering you that much that you would just leave?" The way he said it sounded...almost heartbroken and Phainon waved his hands almost to banish the idea.

"No! No!" He protested, leaning forward a little. Mydei's hot skin felt burning even from a few inches away. His hand gently touched the other's knee, the warm skin making his body want to shiver. "I just - you keep looking for me like I'm going to hurt you."

Mydei's ears pulled back, a grimace on his face. "It's nothing of the sort. We just pay attention when we're...under such conditions." The way he said it...it was like choosing words carefully. Like he knew what was wrong but he knew Phainon's panic and that saying it aloud would only make it worse. Yet, it panicked him seeing Mydei struggle in his sleep, small little whines leaving his throat in pure distress.

"So you know what it is?"

"Unfortunately I figured it out this morning. It hasn't happened before so I'm just...learning. Hybrids can get like this...sometimes." His quiet reasoning did nothing but amplify Phainon's panic. He knew what was wrong and he wouldn't let Phainon help. It frustrated him, it made him angry that Mydei felt like he couldn't trust him. Phainon trusted Mydei with every part of him. Coveted him. Sure, he may even be called 'down bad' - but Mydei was always closed off and guarded.
